requirement:
An mdBook chapter MAY declare a named definition using a fenced `{definition}` directive. Definitions MUST use the same chapter-qualified names, identifier rules, fence rules, and nonempty-body rules as requirements and examples. Names MUST be unique across all three kinds.

Each definition MUST declare exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before its explanatory body. The phrase MUST be interpreted as plain text. Definitions MUST NOT require their own evidence records or determinations.
rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation in `requirements.definitions.declaration` has code that carries it out and a test that exercises it.

**Shared name, identifier and fence rules**
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]` parses `{definition}` blocks with the same `definition_blocks` function used for requirements and examples. That function is `src/lib.rs#fn[definition_blocks]`.
- It applies `full_requirement_name` and `valid_name` to every kind, so names are chapter-qualified and follow the same identifier rules.
- It reports an unclosed fence ("missing a closing colon fence") for all kinds.
- Fence-length handling in `definition_blocks` is also shared.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[preprocess_book]` applies the same name validity check when building the rendered book.
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence]` covers a longer fence that holds a shorter colon line, and an invalid chapter-qualified name (`bad dir.terms.a`).
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported]` covers the missing closing fence.

**Unique names across the three kinds**
- `collect_definitions` keeps one `definitions` map for all kinds. A second declaration with the same name gets a "duplicate definition/requirement/example …" error.
- `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` declares a `{req} x` and then a `{definition} x`, and asserts the "duplicate definition bad.x" error.

**Exactly one nonempty `:phrase:` option before a nonempty body**
- `src/terms.rs#fn[declaration]` requires the first line to be `:phrase:` with a nonempty value. It rejects an empty body and a repeated `:phrase:`.
- `collect_definitions` calls it for `DefinitionKind::Term` and reports the error as "definition NAME: …". It also reports "has no text" for empty text.
- `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` calls the same function when rendering.
- `invalid_declarations_and_reference_targets_are_reported` covers four bad bodies and asserts a "definition bad.bad:" error for each:
  - no phrase;
  - an empty phrase;
  - two phrases;
  - a phrase with no body.

**Phrase interpreted as plain text**
- `src/terms.rs#fn[escaped_phrase]` is reached from `replace_definitions`. It escapes Markdown and HTML metacharacters.
- `tests/definitions.rs#fn[phrases_are_plain_links_and_markdown_literals_are_preserved]` asserts that `*alpha* & <beta>` renders as `*alpha* & <beta>`, and that the `:phrase:` line is removed from the rendered chapter.

**No evidence records or determinations**
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[inspect_repository_with_progress]` filters out `DefinitionKind::Term` when it decides which evidence files are expected.
- It also skips terms when it reports missing evidence.
- `definitions_share_name_and_fence_rules_and_need_no_evidence` asserts that no error mentions `long.fenced` or `glossary.`, while the requirement `rules.ready` still gets "evidence/rules.ready.json: missing".

All the code that carries out these obligations is reachable from the three {impl} items. Those items are `inspect_repository_with_progress`, `collect_definitions` and `preprocess_book`. All three tests carry {test} references to the subject.
